_what: PL-14 ledger: split test families (2+ suites for one subject) with NO shared testUtils, measured 2026-08-28. Each is a family where every suite re-declares its own setup — the pattern behind the tests-tree duplication and the bulk stale-mock breakages. This list may only SHRINK. A family NOT listed here fails the moment it appears, so new debt cannot be added.
_note: Not every entry is a defect: some families are split for SIZE with genuinely different setup per suite. Those get adjudicated to a reason string when touched; until then they sit here as measured debt. 2026-08-28: four families were ADDED here — not new debt, but debt made visible. Their suites always covered one module from two separate test trees (tests/ and tests/unit/); merging the trees under the ADR-016 placement rule put them side by side, where the shared-setup rule can finally see them. 2026-08-31: `tests/sop/tool` joins `tests/sop/credential` and `tests/sop/no` as a FALSE family — the detector takes everything before the first `-` as a subject, so tool-auth-review and tool-catalog-gating look like one split suite. Three of the sop rows are now this, which is a signal the subject rule is coarser than it reads. 2026-09-02: seven rows LEFT that were never families at all — the grouping keys on a filename's first hyphen-token, so `no-bare-sleep`/`no-config-leaf-mocks`/`no-lowered-test-timeout` read as one family and `securityValidation-*` as another, when they are ten separate subjects. They sat here as debt nobody could pay: there is no shared setup to extract from files that share nothing. The detector now requires a real subject before calling a group a family.

adjudicated.tests/types/typeGuards: Eight suites, and not one has a beforeEach or a jest.mock — these are pure predicates and accessors split by concern (project, mesh, App Builder, EDS, utility). There is no setup to share; the two that need a Project already use the canonical projectFake helper, which is the shared thing.
adjudicated.tests/features/project-creation/handlers: Eleven suites covering separate creation flows. No module is mocked by even half of them and five mock nothing at all, so a shared preamble would be a union nobody needs. The two component-loading suites do overlap; that is a pair, and the Rule of Three says leave it.
adjudicated.tests/features/project-creation/ui/wizar: Four suites over pure helpers — navigation, state-config, store structure — with zero module mocks between them. Nothing to extract.
adjudicated.tests/core/utils/projectDisplayName: Two suites over a pure formatter. No mocks, no beforeEach; the split is by input class, and each case is its own arrange line.
adjudicated.tests/core/shell/commandSequencer: The helpers suite covers pure sequencing functions and the base suite covers the sequencer itself. Zero module mocks between them, so the only thing they could share is an import.
adjudicated.tests/core/ui/components/wizard/Configur: A rendering suite and a helpers suite. The helpers are pure and mock nothing; the render suite needs Spectrum stubs the helpers suite must not have.
adjudicated.tests/features/project-creation/ui/steps: Three suites with zero module mocks between them — the predicates half is pure and the render halves stub only what each renders, which is the per-suite rule the Spectrum preamble convention asks for.
adjudicated.tests/features/mesh/services/meshCheckHe: Three suites over three separate helper predicates (API Mesh enablement, the fallback path, mesh existence). One module mocked across the whole family, and each suite drives a different collaborator.
adjudicated.tests/features/eds/services/configGenera: Four suites over four independent generation concerns — config flags, the golden mesh endpoint, component-config merging, and generation itself. One module mocked in total across the family.
adjudicated.tests/core/state/projectFileLoader: Five suites, each pinning a different migration or warning path (DA.live site, orphaned configs, package migration, shape-warning dedup). One module mocked across all five; the fixtures differ per suite because the whole point of each is a differently-malformed file.
adjudicated.tests/features/prerequisites/handlers/sh: Five suites over separate exported helpers — dependency resolution, plugin Node versions, node mapping, per-node status, required versions. Two module mocks in total across the family and no common one.
adjudicated.tests/features/eds/handlers/storefrontSe: Two suites sharing no mocked module at all, out of twelve mocked between them: the auth half stubs the credential chain, the base half stubs the file and repo operations. A shared preamble would be the union of two disjoint sets.
adjudicated.tests/features/dashboard/handlers/config: Three suites sharing no mocked module at all: the store-structure half stubs one collaborator, the secrets half stubs none, and the base half stubs four. Their intersection is empty, so a shared preamble would be a union.
adjudicated.tests/features/lifecycle/services/projec: Two suites with an empty intersection — the component-list half mocks nothing and the mesh-context half mocks seven modules to reach the deploy path. There is no common ground to lift.
adjudicated.tests/features/dashboard/commands/showDa: Three suites over separate behaviours (auto-reopen, push targets, the command itself) with two mocked modules in total and none in common.
adjudicated.tests/features/projects-dashboard/ui/Pro: Two render suites split for size, sharing one mocked module. Spectrum stubs are per-suite by convention, each mocking only what its own tree renders, so lifting them would force both to carry the primitives of the other.
adjudicated.tests/features/project-creation/ui/steps: Three suites: a pure predicates half, a footer render half, and the step itself. One mocked module across all three.
adjudicated.tests/features/eds/ui/steps/RepoSelectio: Five suites, each pinning a different repo-selection outcome (app check, create success, default branch, readiness). Two mocked modules across the family and none shared; the arrange differs because the outcome under test differs.
adjudicated.tests/features/eds/ui/steps/repoSelectio: Two suites over the code-sync helpers, sharing no mocked module. The upper-case sibling entry is a different subject: the component, not the helpers.
adjudicated.tests/features/eds/services/storefront/s: Two suites with zero mocked modules between them; the generator-coupling half is a pure comparison and the base half drives the detector directly.
adjudicated.tests/features/project-creation/handlers: Two suites sharing no mocked module: the auth-guard half stubs the guard chain, the base half drives the flow with collaborators handed in.
adjudicated.tests/features/project-creation/services: Two suites split for size, one covering the isolation rule and the other the refresh itself, with no mocked module in common.
adjudicated.tests/features/project-creation/ui/compo: Two render suites split for size with one mocked module between them. The Spectrum stubs differ because each renders a different part of the gallery.
adjudicated.tests/types/webview: Two suites over pure type guards with zero mocked modules; the error-codes half is a table-driven check over a constant.
adjudicated.tests/features/authentication/handlers/w: Two suites mocking the same single module. That is a pair, not a family: the Rule of Three applies, and the measurement puts the whole saving at three lines.
adjudicated.tests/features/ai/mcpDriftDetector: Two suites split by scope, global versus project, with two mocked modules between them and none in common, because each scope reads a different config.
adjudicated.tests/core/shell/processCleanup: Five suites split by test STRATEGY, not size: three drive REAL child processes and raise the jest timeout to survive scheduler contention, two mock tree-kill outright. A shared preamble would push a tree-kill mock into the suites whose entire claim is that a real process actually dies. The measured duplication is the ten-line comment explaining the raised timeout, repeated three times — documentation, not setup, and less discoverable if hidden in a helper.
adjudicated.tests/core/validation/fieldValidation: Three suites over pure validators, one per field. No beforeEach, no jest.mock, and the only import is the subject itself. There is nothing to share.
adjudicated.tests/types/demoPackages: Two suites over pure type guards, importing only the subject. No setup exists.
adjudicated.tests/features/eds/services/errorFormatt: Two suites over pure formatters with no mocks and no beforeEach. The one that needs an error already uses the canonical codedErrorFake helper, which is the shared thing.
adjudicated.tests/commands/diagnostics: Two suites over different halves of the diagnostics command — the report copier and the credential probe — with no mocked modules and no common collaborator. Only one needs a beforeEach at all.
